import nanosurf

# Load application
spm = nanosurf.SPM()
application = spm.application

# Get variables
scan = application.Scan
zcontrol = application.ZController

# Check available properties for zcontrol
print("Z Controller properties:")
zcontrol_props = [prop for prop in dir(zcontrol) if not prop.startswith('_')]
for prop in zcontrol_props:
    print(f"  {prop}")

# Check if DGain exists
if hasattr(zcontrol, 'DGain'):
    print(f"\nDGain exists! Current value: {zcontrol.DGain}")
else:
    print("\nDGain property not found")

del spm
"}

import nanosurf

# Load application
spm = nanosurf.SPM()
application = spm.application

# Get variables
scan = application.Scan
zcontrol = application.ZController

# Set PID gains
zcontrol.PGain = 100
zcontrol.IGain = 6000
zcontrol.DGain = 10

# Set scanning parameters
scan.Scantime = 0.1  # Time per line in seconds
scan.Lines = 128  # Lines per frame

print("Parameters set successfully!")
print(f"P Gain: {zcontrol.PGain}")
print(f"I Gain: {zcontrol.IGain}")
print(f"D Gain: {zcontrol.DGain}")
print(f"Time per Line: {scan.Scantime} s")
print(f"Lines per Frame: {scan.Lines}")

del spm
"}

The lower P gain (100) and D gain (10) provide gentler feedback control, while the moderate I gain (6000) maintains stable tracking. The fast scan time (0.1 s per line) with 128 lines per frame allows for efficient scanning while reducing the total time the tip is in contact with the sample surface.
